06/ 10.09.2015
.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the opposite parties.

2.  The petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated 10.04.2008 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jamshedpur, in C/2 Case No. 685 of 2008, whereby cognizance has been taken against the petitioner for the offence under Section 16(1)(a) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (herein after referred to as the 'Act').
The petitioner has also prayed for quashing the entire criminal proceeding against him in the said C/2 Case No. 685 of 2008.
3. The prosecution report has been brought on record, which shows that the sample of bread was taken from the general food shop of the petitioner, which was found to be misbranded.
The analysis report has also been brought on record which shows that the bread was not labeled in accordance with Rule 32 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and hence it was misbranded.
With these allegations the persecution report was filed, on the basis of which the cognizance was taken by the Court below.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has taken a simple point challenging the impugned order,
submitting that while taking the sample from the shop of the petitioner the procedure prescribed under Rule 11(1)(a) of the Act was not followed and no notice was given to the petitioner about the intention to have the sample analysed.

Learned counsel accordingly, submitted that since no notice under Section 11(1)(a) of the Act was given to the petitioner, the further procedure could not be Ajay Kumar Dadheech vs State Of Jharkhand & Ors on 10 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26882610/
1 followed and accordingly, the impugned order passed by the Court below is absolutely illegal and cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel has submitted that this point has been specifically taken by the petitioner in paragraph-8 of the application, and though the counter affidavit has been filed by the State and it is stated that the procedure prescribed under Section 11 of the Act, had been followed, but no notice has been brought on record.

Learned counsel accordingly,
submitted that the impugned order, as also the entire criminal proceeding against the petitioner, are absolutely illegal, and cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
5. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the prayer and has submitted that on the basis of the prosecution report, the offence is clearly made out against the petitioner.
However, it is admitted by learned counsel for the State that the notice under Section 11(1)(a) of the Act is not available.

6. Section 11(1)(a) of the Act reads as follows:-
"11. Procedure to be followed by Food Inspectors.- (1) When a Food Inspector takes a sample of food for analysis, he shall- (a) give notice in writing then and there of his intention to have it so analysed to the person from whom he has taken the sample and to the person, if any, whose name,
address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A;"
7.

A bare reading of Section 11(1)(a) of the Act clearly shows that this Section is mandatory in nature,
which is required to be followed and if the prescribed procedure under section 11(1)(a) of the Act is not followed at the time of collecting the sample, the prosecution cannot stand in the eyes of law.
8.

In the facts of this case, as the State is not in a position to bring on record the notice prescribed under Section 11(1)(a) of the Act, it has to be construed that no such notice was given to the petitioner at the time of taking the sample from his shop.
Accordingly, the impugned order, as also the entire criminal proceeding against the petitioner, cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

9. For the aforementioned reasons, the impugned order dated 10.04.2008 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jamshedpur, in C/2 Case No. 685 of 2008, as also the entire criminal proceeding against the petitioner in the said case, are hereby, quashed.
This application is accordingly, allowed.

(H.C.Mishra, J.) D.S.
